full_judgment: 2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted other Suit No. 68 of 1994 in the 2nd Court of the Subordinate Judge. Nilphamari impleading the opposite parties defendants praying for a decree for declaration of title to the suit land and structures standing thereon, as described in the schedule `kha' out of schedule `ka' of the plaint. The plaintiff asserted that the suit land originally belonged to one Jamuna Prosad Saha. Ranneswar Prosad Saha and others and white in possession over 'ka' schedule property they got their names recorded in the CS Khatian in 1340 BS and thereafter Raj Kishore Prasad died leaving behind his wife Moneswari Saha and daughter Bhuipi Debi Saha as heirs and ultimately Jamuna Prosad Saha and others renamed as owner of the suit land and that during the SA operation got their names duly recoded in the SA Khatian in 1962 and Jamuna Prosad Saha was possessing the suit land. Thereafter Jamuna Prosad Saha transferred the suit land by a registered kabala No. 11060 on 25-3-63 in favour of the plaintiff who was then a minor and possession was taken on his behalf by his father and that after the death of his father the plaintiff himself began to look after the suit land. It is further case of the plaintiff that one Anwar Ali Bepari father of the defendant No. 1 was the tenant under the plaintiff in the suit land and after his death in 1981 the defendant No. 4 has been in possession in the suit land as a tenant under the plaintiff. The plaintiff then asserted that while in possession through the tenant the plaintiff went to the local Tahsil office and learnt on 30-12-92 that the suit land has been enlisted as vested and non resident property and the defendant No. 4 obtained lease of the suit land in VP Case No. 2 of 1971. According to the plaintiff the suit land can never be vested and non resident property and plaintiff title has been condoned by the alleged treatment of the suit land as vested and non resident property hence the suit.
